_comment: K3 fixed-seed demonstration campaign, DEFAULT Castalia config.
Six streams, chosen so that each one has a job no other one does:
k3s01/k3s02  profile 'seq'  -- the roadmap Step 2 sequencer weighting
(div/AMO/LR-SC).  k3s01 is the lockstep
candidate; k3s02 is a second seed so the
behavioral result is not a single sample.
k3b01        profile 'base' -- flat weighting, the widest class mix.
k3z01        profile 'bitm' -- Zba/Zbb/Zbs/Zbc heavy, the widest decode
surface on this config.
k3i01        profile 'irq'  -- CLINT self-injection WITH the epilogue
handler-count assertion.  Behavioral only:
the reference never executes the bracketed
handler, so the count word it would read is
stale on the reference side by design.
k3i02        profile 'irq'  -- the same axis WITHOUT the count assertion,
which is what makes it lockstep-eligible
(BRACKET_ISR=1).  Weaker behavioral verdict,
stronger oracle.  The pair is the point.
Seeds are arbitrary but FIXED and recorded; R-DK5 requires the reproduction
line, not a particular value.
RE-RECORDED 2026-08-23, config digest 9ca2e20fb3d2 -> 1ffadbaf4c85.
The recorded hashes are over the WHOLE .S, and the .S header carries the
resolved-config identity, so a config default flip moves every hash even
when no instruction moves.  Two flips landed after the 2026-08-03 record:
52130ac (priv.trapCsr on by default) and e9ece88/1af1953 (numHarts 4->5,
Castalia Penta).  Measured before re-recording: the current generator
reproduces all six 2026-08-03 hashes byte for byte when handed the
2026-08-03 resolved config, and the only difference between old-config and
new-config output is the one `# config :` comment line per file.  A future
mismatch at an UNCHANGED digest is the opposite finding -- the generator
moved -- and must not be re-recorded without an explanation.
Regenerate with:
/usr/bin/python3.6 tools/randgen/randgen.py campaign --spec <this file>
and check reproducibility with `randgen.py verify`.
